To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Perceived control and fairness influence consumers’ satisfaction through their effect on consumers’ contingent self-esteem (i.e. their need to feel good about themselves) and their trust in the service provider.”
perceived fairness and control influence consumers’ satisfaction through the mediation of their CSE and their trust.
consumers’ satisfaction with a service encounter is influenced by their perceptions of control and the fairness of the exchange, their CSE and their trust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of psychological processes that guide consumer’s satisfaction evaluations.
the role of CSE and trust as mediators between service encounter attributes (control and fairness) and consumers’ satisfaction evaluations.
the psychological processes that influence consumer satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSE is a significant mediator between service encounters, satisfaction and behavioral intentions.
consumers’ satisfaction evaluations are affected by their perceptions of fairness in the service interaction and their CSE and their trust in the service provider.
consumers’ satisfaction evaluations are a function of the extent to which they feel in control of and treated fairly during a service encounter.   1
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
service providers should design service interactions that affirm the self-concept and thereby improve satisfaction.
consumers’ satisfaction evaluations are influenced by their perceptions of fairness, control, and self-esteem.

the service providers should design service interactions that are not only fair, but also provide consumers with a feeling of control over the service encounter and thereby improves consumers’ CSE, trust and satisfaction evaluations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
service encounters should be designed to enhance consumers’ perceptions of self-control and fairness in the transaction.
service providers should strive to design service interactions that affirm consumer’s self-image and thereby improve satisfaction evaluations.
service providers should design service encounters to enhance consumer’s CSE and trust perceptions.
